# Faceless Champ

> Python 3.12+ video authoring library. Manim-style scenes, Pillow frames, FFmpeg MP4.

- [Quickstart](README.md)
- [API](docs/api.md)
- [Timing, composition, audio, troubleshooting](docs/guide.md)
- [Renderer and timeline architecture](docs/architecture.md)
- [Runnable examples](examples/showcase.py)
- [Authoring skill](skills/faceless-champ/SKILL.md)

Import from faceless_champ. Subclass Scene and override construct(). Use add(),
play(), wait(), and add_audio(). Coordinates are design pixels, top-left origin,
positive Y down; component anchors default to center. play() advances time and runs
its arguments concurrently. Audio start defaults to the current cursor, not zero.
Export with render() or faceless-champ render file.py SceneName -o output.mp4.
Use Sequence for cuts/crossfades and Grid for simultaneous row-major panels.
Grid supports padding and start_times for staggered panels; offsets apply to audio.
Layer composites transparent canvases in order for shared headings and overlays.
Equation typesets TeX-style expressions with the optional equations extra; Write
reveals formulas without changing their layout. Polyline draws curves and closed
filled paths. Rectangle supports corner_radius. The one-minute example is in
training project/equation-render/render.py and its scene/ directory.
ColorScheme.named("midnight"/"paper"/"ocean") supplies reusable visual roles;
with_alpha() creates shaded fills. Equation.color_map colors individual symbols
and Greek commands without reflow; matching glyphs anywhere receive their colors.
Polyline(line_cap="round") supports smooth graph endpoints. Text.font_weight sets
the Weight axis of an explicit variable font; omit it for a static font.
Use SubtitleTrack.from_srt() for exact cue times, Captions for word highlighting,
and with scene.at(time) for absolute scheduling. Add captions at zero for source
audio timestamps. Use Arrow for drawable connectors and Icon for tinted PNGs.
wait_until() advances to an absolute time; remove() ends a visual's lifetime.
Motion presets: SlideIn/Out, ZoomIn/Out, PopIn/Out, BounceIn, SpinIn, Pulse, Shake,
and Wiggle. Animation supports keyframes and relative transform values. Explicit
play(rate_func=...) overrides preset easing; default easing falls back to smooth.
The narrated example is in training project/good-math/render.py and scene/story.py.
Charts include BarChart, RankedBarChart, LineChart, ScatterPlot, Histogram, Heatmap,
NetworkGraph, SankeyChart, VectorField, and PieChart. See docs/charts.md.
RankedBarChart accepts category-to-value mappings, including None for missing data.
Use .animate.data_to() for interpolated ranks and values with stable category colors.
Ranked bar axes adjust automatically unless fixed with x_axis=Axis(limits=(0, max)).
Number(value, format_spec=",.0f", prefix="", suffix="", formatter=None, width=None)
inherits Text options and supports .animate.value_to(value), including signed values.
The 45-second light-mode example is training project/company-growth/render.py.
ChartStyle accepts font/font_weight and title_font/title_font_weight, sharing Text
font validation. line_width sets chart stroke width. RankedBarChart accepts bar_height,
corner_radius, and show_markers. LineChart(end_labels=True) labels final series points.
Ellipse(width=..., height=...) is a drawable Shape with independent dimensions.
The company-growth example follows layout.png with ivory, serif fonts, and fine line art.
render(progress=callback) reports completed and total frame counts for render feedback.
No camera, video import, or graphical editor in v0.1.
